Messages.Author: Shawn F. Carnes
Messages.Body:
An update for those who are interested:

We are currently re-working the V:TES tournament rules for the DCI, and
**possibly** adding some variant tournaments.

Now, I know the SPTR (Sensible Player's Tournament Rules), and there are
thinks I like and dislike about it... (can you see the opinion hat being
donned?) but for every one think I dislike about the SPTR, there are at
least two or three things I like. It is player friendly, that much is
for sure. I don't think, however, that a modified SPTR would work with
the DCI, nor do I think the SPTR creators want that either.

With this in mind, and if you care, what changes would *YOU* like to see
in the current DCI tournament rules for V:TES? Please keep them to this
thread.

Thanks!

>
>With this in mind, and if you care, what changes would *YOU* like to see
>in the current DCI tournament rules for V:TES? Please keep them to this
>thread.

I'm not trying to argue or attack your judgement, but I would like to know
why you prefer DC rules to SPTR. I, the people I know, and this group,
much prefer SPTR.

2 big issues for DC:

1) The fix for weenie vote push (WVP) is not adequate. Weenie vote is
still necessarily better than any other vote deck, as there are dozens of
votes to dump into the deck and use to ram through the votes that count..
Single vote push (SVP) from the SPTR fixes it fine, and is the consensus
"best fix" on this group. If you can't abide rules changes and must fix
it with some kind of card limit, you need to switch from 6-card limits on
certain vote cards to a percentage restriction on the total number of
votes in the deck (I suggest 40%).

2) Jyhad/V:tES games are often long. The time limits should reflect this.
I can't see a limit less than 1/2 hour per player; otherwise it's no
longer Jyhad/V:tES.

In addition the 6-card limit on certain untap cards is virtually
guaranteed to be inadequate once Sabbat is out. Once a deck has 4
different untaps (24 total) it can already do endless bleed. Probably it
would be a good idea to alter that fix now as well, rather than being
forced into a change later.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 30 Jul 1996, Shawn F. Carnes wrote:

> An update for those who are interested:

> We are currently re-working the V:TES tournament rules for the DCI, and
> **possibly** adding some variant tournaments.

Hmm... What do you mean by variant tournaments? "Duels" (ug), different
victory conditions? This is unclear.

> Now, I know the SPTR (Sensible Player's Tournament Rules), and there are
> thinks I like and dislike about it... (can you see the opinion hat being
> donned?) but for every one think I dislike about the SPTR, there are at
> least two or three things I like.

As the original author of the SPTR, I invite you and anyone else to
privately e-mail (or post on a different thread) me any concerns you
have, what you like, and what you dislike. The rules are in constant
revision and always looking to achieve fairness.
(<http://cslab.uwlax.edu/~sulli_al/jyhad/SPTR,html) for those who don't
know where it is)

> It is player friendly, that much is
> for sure. I don't think, however, that a modified SPTR would work with
> the DCI, nor do I think the SPTR creators want that either.

Well, actually, the SPTR was created in the hopes that it would wake up
those in DCI to making a useful tournament rules set. Basicly, I want
the SPTR to be a creation with planned obselesence(sp?).

> With this in mind, and if you care, what changes would *YOU* like to see
> in the current DCI tournament rules for V:TES? Please keep them to this
> thread.

QUITE a few:

I know full well that many things the DCI cannot change with regards to
V:tES. There is a large problem with the DCI rules as written:
They require everyone to play "nice" or they break.

Good rules for any system should not require someone to say, "Well, you
can make whatever you want within the rules, but please don't do this or
my game breaks".

- For the current rules, Weenie Vote Push (WVP) is still
unanswered. A 2CL are about all that hamstring WVP, or creating decks
specifically designed to combat weenie vote push. Unfortunately, this
hamstrings deck creation. You can't just get away with vote defense,
bleed defense, and combat defense in DCI. Once Jyhad slips down that
slope towards necessitating defenses to _specific_ decks, the balance has
been lost. Without Vote pushing, there is no problem, decks can be decks
without having to consider specific individual problems.
Unfortunately, the DCI doesn't have the authority to change vote
push rules (AFAIK). What then, can be done? A 2CL-Restricted list on
damage votes ends the problem, but creates handfuls more. 3CL-Restricted
list still allows the problem. Then there is the added damage of
destroying totally viable decks in the "solving" of the problem. In
order to combat one deck type, too many non-problem decks are then
unmakeable.
As far as I can tell, this problem is pervasive to the current
rulings on vote push, and can't be solved unless these rulings are
changed (outside DCI jurisdiction).
- Time limit
There is simply not enough time in DCI to finish games well. The
rules encourage players to not build combat decks and other, slower
decks, while giving a large advantage to those decks that should burn out.
Solution: Increase the time limit by some X amount.
- Paralyze
Why ban it?
- Things NOT to do
- Sideboards. In a game like Jyhad, this is too horribly
effective. Clan hosers are extremely powerful if used at the right
times, and allowing sideboards would make the finals a competition of who
can screw who more, rather than who has the best deck.
- Card limits. The game becomes something else entirely in a CL
environment.
- Gimicky "alternative" rules. This will do nothing but make a
standard in Jyhad even farther from reality.

For the most part, the flaw in the current DCI tournament rules is that
it uses an ineffective means (a Restricted-list CL) to fix some problems
basic to Jyhad (solved by the Golden Tenets or variants of the GT). If
only DCI could change those, there really wouldn't be a problem.

Shawn, welcome aboard.
Your opinions regarding the SPTR would be highly appreciated.

1) No card limits. Card limits are for broken games.

2) No restricted list. Ditto.

3) Banned list is fine - keep out the "friendly-play-only" cards like
Monocle, et. al.

With this in mind, however, the game itself will have to be fixed, so that
it is not a broken game (otherwise, you need card limits of some kind as
a crutch).

Fixing vote pushing:

1) (Obvious): no vote pushing.
or
2) ..??

Fix infinite combos:

1) (Obvious): no repeat actions.
or
2) a. No self-directed 5th tradition
b. Any "strike:combat ends and untap" effect will not untap an acting
minion until the end of the current turn (or miniion phase).
(this still allows pair of Princes to swap 5th traditions infinitely,
and for a Restoration/Freak Drive loop, but these are at least a little
more difficult to pull off than just packing a deck full of Majesties)

I would love to see the restrictions on card backings removed. Removing the
restrictions on the crypt would be a welcome ruling to all of us who
purchased tons of Jyhad cards. When you consider that VTES, Dark Sov. and
AH (Sabbat too, probably) have backings that are distinguishable you see
that it really isn't that important if Jyhad backs are added to the list.

If player X marks their library by playing certain card backs, this pattern
could be recognized by other players who may pick up on the pattern and know
what player X's next library card is. It really doesn't matter that much.

If you can't go with any of this, the least you should do is allow cards
(library and/or crypt) to be double-packed into sleeves so that its not an
issue.

Also, I'd love to see the No Repeat Actions portion of the SPTR included in
the DCI rules. The SPTR uses this as a way of eliminating the need for card
limits on cards like Majesty and Earth Meld. I, however, would like to see
the limit on these cards remain in effect so that we dont see anymore decks
load with S:CE cards.

The truth is, I'm one of the sickos who actually _like_ the DCI rules. My
playgroup has been playing with them for months and have even attended some
Los Angeles area tournaments run with them.

NOTE: Make sure the *%&^#$%'s at the DC put the new rules on the Web page
and in their sanctioning packets this time. As of 2 weeks ago, the
sanctioning packet was still using the Nov'95 DCI rules!

Messages.Author: Alec Chang
Messages.Body:
Shawn F. Carnes wrote:
>
> An update for those who are interested:

> **possibly** adding some variant tournaments.

> Now, I know the SPTR (Sensible Player's Tournament Rules), and there are

> least two or three things I like. It is player friendly, that much is

> the DCI, nor do I think the SPTR creators want that either.
>

> With this in mind, and if you care, what changes would *YOU* like to see
> in the current DCI tournament rules for V:TES? Please keep them to this
> thread.

1) Lose the restrictions on the card backs that players can use in their
crypts. All the expansions are differentiable just at a glance, so it
really doesn't matter anyway.

2) Reduce the restricted list to as few cards as possible. Jyhad was
made for NL. The only cards that I'd want to see stay on it would be
Freak Drive and Hospitality.

3) Do not adopt the "No Repeat Actions" part of the SPTR unless
absolutely necessary. Deal with Fortitude Infinite loops(with Freak
Drive) another way, please. S:CE untaps are not nearly as ridiculous,
and in my experience do not unbalance the game and can be dealt with in
multiple ways.

4) Ban Archon Investigation. This one card provides bleed defense for
any deck, requires no skill to play, is excessively harsh on the affected
bleeder(burning is way too much...), and hoses an entire strategy. As
such, it should not be allowed in tournaments unless errated or altered.

5)Take the cards from Jyhad which use "Paralyze" off of the banned list.

Good luck with your time as Netrep, and keep practicing your fortitude...

Alec Chang

Messages.Author: Charles T. Schwope
Messages.Body:
"Shawn F. Carnes" <sw...@castle.wizards.com> wrote:

>Now, I know the SPTR (Sensible Player's Tournament Rules), and there are
>thinks I like and dislike about it... (can you see the opinion hat being
>donned?) but for every one think I dislike about the SPTR, there are at
>least two or three things I like. It is player friendly, that much is
>for sure. I don't think, however, that a modified SPTR would work with
>the DCI, nor do I think the SPTR creators want that either.

I think many players find the SPTR the best set of rules out there.
Personally I would like to see that in place as the official rule set.

>With this in mind, and if you care, what changes would *YOU* like to see
>in the current DCI tournament rules for V:TES? Please keep them to this
>thread.

There are a couple of problems with the current DC rules (IMHO).
1. Vote push. This is a serious problem. I look at the DCI rules
and know that a weenie vote push deck will win at any table that does
not have another WVP at it. A WVP that I put together under the DCI
rules for use in 10%CL enviro swept a table relatively easily. Vote
push is broken, and does not make any sense in an "real world"
reality. (How exactly are my 3 catiff's out voting 3 princes?)
2. Repeat actions. This I am not as sure about b/c no one in our
group has made an ugly repeat action deck. But I have seen glimpses
of this problem from time to time, and any deck dedicated to doing
just that will be nasty nasty nasty. Without vote push, I can see the
gangrel untap and bleed decks being too dominant.
3. Time limits. I have no idea how to fix this, but the current
limit is way to short. I can count on my hands the number of times
I've seen a VTES game end in less then 2 hours. At the very least
make it so you have a full 2 hours of play time, if not 2 1/2 hours at
the least. It may not make much of a difference, but it may make some
difference.
4. Table set up. I would like to see it set up in a semi-swiss
style. You end up at a table with other people who are doing as well
as you are. I think this is more fair for more players, and if it is
a 3 round minimum before the finals, it should work out ok. I could
also see just a pure 4 round system with no finals if you do it in a
swiss style. I haven't looked at how points jump in VTES tourneys,
but fixing the scoring system so that it would work well with swiss
would be ideal. I think it already works well with swiss, and being
as I'm a huge swiss style fan (from playing in MtG tourneys) I would
like to see it done for VTES as well.

Charles

Messages.Author: Algustas
Messages.Body:
Hi Shawn,
Oh yes, one other burning problem: Wake With Evenings Freshness.
This card can be terribly abused, not because of what it does, but
because there is really no penalty for overstaking your deck with them.
Other cards, (vote pushing aside), are self-limiting in numbers, because
if you put too many in you jam your hand with them when you don't want
them. As it stands with WWEF, you can through away one per tapped minion
anytime anyone other than yourself takes an action. Almost any serious
Jyhad group has some sort of house rule for this card. PLEASE do not
restrict it to six per deck, as you will ruin many viable, non-abusive
strategies. The groups I play with use a house rule allowing you to play
a WWEF only when you actually attempt to block or when you are playing a
reaction card.

In my view, at least, untap-bleed and repeat actions are not so much of
a problem as to make them restricted. Freak Drive and Infinite Loop are
abusive, but penalizing all repeat actions for the power of one or two cards
seems way too harsh.
The conditions set making all bleeds different actions prevent the
use of one major bleed strategy that _isn't_ stealth. There are three main bleed
strategies-Stealth, Tap, and Intimidation. Intimidation is the most unreliable,
and relies on Combat as well, i.e. Tremere/Brujah Bruise-Bleed. Tap is slightly
more reliable, and the typical Ventrue bleed uses Misdirections and Consanguineous
Condemnations to disable blockers. Stealth is the most reliable, usually using
Obfuscate. Anyone say Malks? No repeat actions takes a great deal of power
away from Tap.

well as the abusive ones. This is my deck below, built for 4CL (but the

I wanted to express my concurrence with most of Alex's opinions...

>
> 1) Lose the restrictions on the card backs that players can use in their
> crypts. All the expansions are differentiable just at a glance, so it
> really doesn't matter anyway.

This is probably the most crippling restriction for long time players with
lots of Jyhad, DS, and AH but little VTES. They either have to play a
crypt of all expansion clans, or a crypt of all original Camarilla vamps;
no ICs or new clan members.

If considered essential, you could have crypt draws come off the bottom
(the first four could still come off the top, since they are right after
the cut). Cards that applied to the top of the crypt (e.g. Grendel) would
then apply to the bottom instead and vice versa. The only possible problem
card I can think of is Illusions of the Kindred, since you would be able
to see the card back of the upcoming illusionary Kindred. You could ignore
that or put in a special rule. Unlike the library, drawing from the crypt
is infrequent enough that drawing off the bottom is acceptable.

The library restriction could probably also be loosened to 30/70 or 25/75.

>
> 2) Reduce the restricted list to as few cards as possible. Jyhad was
> made for NL. The only cards that I'd want to see stay on it would be
> Freak Drive and Hospitality.
>
> 3) Do not adopt the "No Repeat Actions" part of the SPTR unless
> absolutely necessary. Deal with Fortitude Infinite loops(with Freak
> Drive) another way, please. S:CE untaps are not nearly as ridiculous,
> and in my experience do not unbalance the game and can be dealt with in
> multiple ways.

Other possibilities:

Restrict offensive untaps to 10 total, rather than 6 of each (and consider
Rutor's Hand an offensive untap). Settites need access to more than 6
Majesties.

Restrict votes to 40% of a deck in total and have no restrictions on
individual vote cards. The pros/cons of this vs. single Vote Push are
being discussed in another thread. It's a deck composition restriction
rather than a rule change, which the DCI may be more amenable to.

>
> 4) Ban Archon Investigation. This one card provides bleed defense for
> any deck, requires no skill to play, is excessively harsh on the affected
> bleeder(burning is way too much...), and hoses an entire strategy. As
> such, it should not be allowed in tournaments unless errated or altered.

Amen.

>
> 5)Take the cards from Jyhad which use "Paralyze" off of the banned list.

Yes, why not?

>
> Good luck with your time as Netrep, and keep practicing your fortitude...
>

I hope you're not limited to 6 Skin of Steel. :-)

> Alec Chang

On Thu, 1 Aug 1996, Nathan Harada wrote:

> In my view, at least, untap-bleed and repeat actions are not so much of
> a problem as to make them restricted. Freak Drive and Infinite Loop are
> abusive, but penalizing all repeat actions for the power of one or two cards
> seems way too harsh.

> use of one major bleed strategy that _isn't_ stealth. There are three
> main bleed strategies-Stealth, Tap, and Intimidation. Intimidation is
> the most unreliable, and relies on Combat as well, i.e. Tremere/Brujah
> Bruise-Bleed. Tap is slightly more reliable, and the typical Ventrue
> bleed uses Misdirections and Consanguineous Condemnations to disable
> blockers.

Tap is still highly effective in GT. Misdirection, Cons. Condemnation
are still usable. S:CE or Freaky Untaps can be used after other
threatening actions (attempt to equip or use an Ivenrary Scotland...).
The problem lies in what can be done with repeat actions, not what can
not be done. While a "tap and bleed deck" will not be as effective, I can
personally attest to the power of a "tap and bleed/vote deck". My
Gangrel version sweeps most tables that aren't ready for it.

> Stealth is the most reliable, usually using Obfuscate.
> Anyone say Malks? No repeat actions takes a great deal of power away
> from Tap.

The question becomes this: are you willing to trade in an abusive game
environment for a minimal loss of some focus in a few non-degenerate
decks? Losing repeat actions is not much of a blow in most decks, and
causes creation of decks that generally do a slightly more broad range of
things in order to offensively reuse their untap, or decks that are more
defensive with their S:CE. Keeping repeat actions, however, allows
abusive combos to be introduced.

> I like SPTR: NL is fine. However, the GT's restrict moderate players as
> well as the abusive ones. This is my deck below, built for 4CL (but the
> proportions would be the same in NL). Call it degenerate all you want, but
> it works on a solid and valid strategy.

I wouldn't call it degenerate. The amount of untappers you include are
not enough to be consistent and nowhere near enough to be considered
abusive. Here is the deck I would not want to see (under current DCI):

Masters:
Information Highway 3
Fame 4
Blood Doll 3
Anarch Revolt 4
Zoo Hunting Ground 1
Misdirection 8

Earth Meld 6
Form of Mist 6
Freak Drive 6
Horrific Countenance 3
Inverary Scotland 2
Palatial Estate 1
Change of Target 3
Earth Control 7
Force of Will 8
Movement of the Slow Body 7
Rapid Healing 8
80 Cards.

Crypt
Badger(x2) 6 PRO FOR
Basilia 10 PRO FOR -- Primogen, Aggravated Hand Damage
Camille Devereux 5(x3) PRO FOR
Gitane St. Clair 7 PRO FOR -- Primogen
Ingrid Rossler 9(x2) FOR PRO -- Prince of Geneva, two extra transfers
Iliana 7 FOR PRO -- No contracts on Iliana
Chandler Hungerford(x2) 3 PRO -- +1 int. vs. GAN
6.25 Average. (High, but other than chandler, only two-ish minions are
needed)

This deck doesn't take long to set up, and once going, it ousts quickly.

Alec's response will likely be that intercept decks can and will be able
to stop this. However, the Misdirections are a real necessity, and the
one critical action to stop (Rapid Healing) comes at a base +1 stealth.
Smart players will save their Earth Controls (total +3 stealth) their
Change of Targets and their Horrific Countenance for these actions.
Given that Misdirection will be involved, a typically 3 to 4 card combo
will be needed to have much of a chance to block, coming from a deck
playing against this deck on it's own terms.

A worst case scenario: Anarch revolts, Fame, and Inverary Scotland out early.

Repeat actions are not fit in a balanced environment. Even though
non-degenerate repeat actions exist, outright disallowing them is not
crippling to most non-degenerate decks. One would be hard-pressed to
find a non-degenerate deck that was affected badly. After untapping,
minions can still always perform other actions or stand back for
defense. If decks are made with this premise in mind, they can easily
take advantage of offensive untapping, though they have to do so with
thought, and not mindless repeated constant bleeds. Another advantage is
that defensive S:CE can once again be a consistent part of the game. As
it stands, certain decks (currently most notable: Setites) have little
recourse to combat.

> abusive. Here is the deck I would not want to see (under current DCI):Mmm... I'm not so sure about that. I've played with and against the deck in
question, and it is consistent. Not abusive, certainly. But consistent in
getting it's actions through, via tap, stealth, or whatever other means are
needed.

(deck description snipped for brevity)

> This deck doesn't take long to set up, and once going, it ousts quickly.
>

>However, the Misdirections are a real necessity, and the
> one critical action to stop (Rapid Healing) comes at a base +1 stealth.

> Change of Targets and their Horrific Countenance for these actions.
> Given that Misdirection will be involved, a typically 3 to 4 card combo
> will be needed to have much of a chance to block, coming from a deck

> playing against this deck on it's own terms.Mmmm... Combat defense seems to be limited to the untap cards; and most
determined combat decks will have ways around S:CE. Misdirections being vital
will make it even more expensive to itself in pool than it already is. Political
decks would be able to make hash out of it. (I will admit, however, that I would
not want to see it, much less play against it.)

> A worst case scenario: Anarch revolts, Fame, and Inverary Scotland out early.
>

> Repeat actions are not fit in a balanced environment. Hem. Depends on your definition of "repeat actions". In one of your earlier
posts(I'm afraid that I don't have it on hand right now), I recall you saying
that all bleed actions, regardless of with card or without were considered to be
"repeat actions", whereas no "enter combat" effects were considered to be repeat
actions. The reasoning that I remember(my memory has been deteriorating
recently) was that classing all combat actions into one group would be difficult
and overly restrictive. Doesn't the same kind of logic apply to bleed actions?
As long as a vampire is prohibited from taking the exact same action over and
over again in a turn{same action being defined as the same basic action (which
requires no card) or action card of the same name}, doesn't that take most of the
bite out of infinite bleed decks, including the one listed above? Unless they
are using a very large selection of bleed action cards, which most do not(and
generally cannot without comprimising their 'infinite' bleed status), vampires
wille be restrained to taking one or two bleed actions per turn under normal
circumstances.

Or, in short, I don't have as much of a problem with "no repeat actions" as long
as the vampire is only prohibited from taking the exact same action again that
turn. I'm not absolutely sure if this suggestion will alleviate the problems
you've found in infinite bleed decks(It seems to make the deck listed above less
insane and more vulnerable; perhaps not totally disabled, but I doubt even the
ordinary GT rules totally disable it), which, I will admit, I have not witnessed,
but I don't think that it would allow any real degeneracy. Would people
complain? Yes, but people still complain about S&B. Anyway, that's my best shot
at suggesting anything which would leave the options of offensive untap decks
mainly open while dealing with Infinite loop decks. I'd need to see one in
action before being able to think of much more.

> Even though
> non-degenerate repeat actions exist, outright disallowing them is not

> crippling to most non-degenerate decks. True; it's not totally crippling. Is it a pain for decks which use
unconventional strategies for getting actions through? Yes.

> One would be hard-pressed to

> find a non-degenerate deck that was affected badly. Nathan Harada's deck, as posted. I can think of my Brujah/Toredor/Ventrue bleed
deck, and my Protean/Dominate bleed decks as well. That doesn't strike me as
particularly "hard pressed", I'm afraid.

> After untapping,
> minions can still always perform other actions or stand back for

> defense. But in a deck which is designed to be ruthlessly offensive to survive(all the
decks I mentioned above), bleeding is one of the most effective strategies.
Introducing votes or other actions into a bleed deck thins out the focus,
especially if those cards cannot be passed easily when played(most of my bleed
decks would be hard pressed to mix politics in with a mind to have even temporary
dominance and still retain their functionality).

> If decks are made with this premise in mind, they can easily
> take advantage of offensive untapping, though they have to do so with

> thought, and not mindless repeated constant bleeds. If the S:CE untaps are not the only ways that actions are gotten through,
especially if other effects like Mind numb, Mummy's tongue, and stealth are being
used, it is hardly mindless repeated constant bleeds. Admittedly, this does come
up occasionally. But my suggestion above would make it at least a little less on
the "mindless" end of things.

> Another advantage is
> that defensive S:CE can once again be a consistent part of the game. As
> it stands, certain decks (currently most notable: Setites) have little

> recourse to combat.Since when was defensive S:CE not a reasonably consistent part of the game? I
see it fairly often in my own decks and those of my friends. Often, in my
non-combat decks, it is the primary way of avoiding combat, along with Elysiums.

Hoping he wasn't too incoherent due to lack of sleep,

Alec Chang

Messages.Author: Wallpaper Paste
Messages.Body:
The Corrupter (sull...@cslab.uwlax.edu) wrote:
: Alec Chang wrote:

: > Drive) another way, please. S:CE untaps are not nearly as ridiculous,
: > and in my experience do not unbalance the game and can be dealt with in
: > multiple ways.

: How should they deal with Infinite bleed loops then?

Pummel the bleeder. Potence has the nice Immortal Grapple
which allows potence combat decks to smash would-be untappers
into a delicious pulp. Get a nice big strike in, and hey, maybe
you can burn him with pulled fangs. Then there is the somewhat
overposerful Thoughts Betrayed which allows the larger Tremere
to basically hose a minion of their choice. It is difficult to
keep a bleed loop going with no vampires or no blood on the
vampires (freak drive is costly, after all).

The GT restriction, imo, damages the Gangrel too much, making it
exceedingly difficult to oust their prey, especially with all
the pool factories my play group always uses. The limit is a
step in the right direction, perhaps, but goes as far to the
other side as it started.

Wallpaper Paste
for all those useless cards
